_why: ADR 0174's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The fix was in the parser (Tests/brenda_client.py) and the catcher is the
the empty-organism call must mean 'any organism', so the value that comes
back keeps the organism of the row it came from, and the set-judge's
organism_mismatch, not silence, reports two animals really measured.
Both mutations are restores of the defect, exactly as ADR 0174 describes:
O1 reverts the gate to `is not None`, which turns the any-organism call
back into an exact-organism call matching every row and blanking every
label; O2 deletes the per-row extraction, so no row keeps an organism in
the any-organism branch and the set's organisms collapse to nothing.
The named-organism test is included in the set's `test` command because
ADR 0174 is not only about the sensor: the guard demands every suite the
record cites, and the record explicitly names both tests that moved
(the sensor test rewritten, the named-organism assertion re-pointed).

mutations.description: the any-organism gate is reverted to `is not None`
the per-row organism extraction in the any-organism branch is deleted
